headline: Highest risk is data leakage from opik’s broad network egress into whisper’s audio-file workflow; prompt injection and capability conflict are otherwise limited by missing shared channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: opik can call a REST API and has broad network egress, while whisper only processes audio files and has no clipboard, MCP, or filesystem write path. No shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is only plausible through unusual manual bridging or external wrappers, not by default.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies opik output into whisper prompts or transcripts
IF a wrapper converts audio-file contents into instruction-bearing text before whisper consumes it
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workflows with no copy-paste bridge
Disable any wrapper that turns opik output into prompt text
Review opik outputs before reuse in downstream transcription tasks
Use a fixed schema for any handoff text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent handoffs

B_data_leakage.rationale: opik’s broad network egress creates a plausible exfiltration path if it receives sensitive audio-derived content, while whisper is local-only with no network egress and only audio-file input. The pair can still leak data through opik’s outbound API calls even though whisper itself does not transmit data.
conditions: IF sensitive audio transcripts are passed from whisper into opik
IF opik forwards transcript content to a third-party REST API
mitigations: Do not send transcripts containing sensitive data to opik
Redact names, IDs, and secrets before any API call
Restrict opik to non-sensitive evaluation corpora
Audit outbound requests from opik for payload contents
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on the REST API boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: whisper cannot write files, modify git, or use MCP, and opik’s profile shows no filesystem write or git mutation either. With no overlapping write surface documented, direct capability conflict is limited to read-only or external orchestration collisions.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF a wrapper adds filesystem or git write permissions not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in shared environments
Separate output directories per agent
Avoid concurrent writes from any wrapper
Check that no hidden git or filesystem permissions are added
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: opik can generate evaluation outputs over REST, and whisper can consume audio files but has no built-in verification or downstream action controls. If whisper-derived text is treated as authoritative by opik or a wrapper, errors can cascade from transcription into evaluation or reporting.
conditions: IF whisper transcripts are fed into opik without human verification
IF opik output is used as ground truth for downstream decisions
mitigations: Insert a human review step between transcription and evaluation
Compare transcripts against source audio for critical cases
Mark opik outputs as provisional, not authoritative
Use confidence thresholds before downstream action
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no stated residency, certification, or retention mismatch. The main compliance concern is limited to any sensitive audio content sent through opik’s networked REST path; whisper itself has no network egress, so it is not the residency driver.
conditions: IF regulated audio or transcripts are sent to opik
IF the REST endpoint stores or processes data outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in opik workflows
Confirm the REST endpoint’s residency and retention terms
Use local-only processing for sensitive audio
Document data handling for transcripts
requires-engineering: add jurisdiction-aware routing
